findings.claim: wordChar tests single bytes and treats only ASCII letters, digits, '_' and '-' as word characters, so a non-ASCII letter right after 'skill' (for example 'skillé') does not end the match and SkillsNamed reports a mention; no test names a Unicode case.
evidence: The diff line `return b == '_' || b == '-' || b >= '0' && b <= '9' || b >= 'a' && b <= 'z' || b >= 'A' && b <= 'Z'` has no branch for bytes >= 0x80.
Role bodies are English and SkillsNamed matches only lowercase ASCII 'skill', so this is unlikely to occur.
Read the full diff of 025ce6ec and engine/gate/skillpaths.go.
The rewrite keeps the indent, trailing spaces and \r: entry is the TrimSpace of the line and strings.Replace(...,1) replaces its first occurrence after the indent.
Adjacent mentions '`a` skill`b` skill' yield both ids; the m[1] < len(body) guard prevents an out-of-range read.
